title: The Simple Tenses
description: Learn the simple present, simple past and simple future for Grade 6: forms, uses and signal words, with bilingual notes, examples, practice exercises and online tests.

topics.title: Simple Present Tense
topics.concept:
The simple present is used for:

  • Habits and routines: She goes to school daily.
  • Universal truths: The sun rises in the east.
  • Permanent states: He lives in Delhi.
  • Fixed timetables: The train leaves at 6 a.m.

Key rule: add -s or -es to the verb for third-person singular (he, she, it):

  • play → plays, go → goes, watch → watches, study → studies.

Signal words: always, usually, often, every day, daily, sometimes, never.

examples.problem: Correct form: She ___ (go) to school by bus.
Why is the present tense used here: Ice melts in heat.?
examples.solution: It states a universal truth, which always takes the simple present.

recap: Used for habits, truths, permanent states, timetables
Signal words: always, usually, every day, never

topics.title: Simple Past Tense
topics.concept:
The simple past describes an action finished at a definite time in the past.

  • Regular verbs add -ed: walk → walked, play → played, stop → stopped.
  • Irregular verbs change: go → went, eat → ate, write → wrote, buy → bought.

The form is the same for all subjects: I/he/we/they went.

Signal words: yesterday, last week, ago, in 2019, then, once.
recap: Used for finished actions at a definite past time
Signal words: yesterday, last…, ago, in 2019

topics.title: Simple Future Tense
topics.concept:
The simple future describes actions that will happen later. Form: will (or shall) + base verb.

  • Predictions: It will rain tomorrow.
  • Promises/decisions: I will help you.
  • Plans: We shall visit Delhi next week.

In modern English will is used with all subjects; shall is more formal and common with I/we. Signal words: tomorrow, next week, soon, later, in the future.
recap: Used for predictions, promises and plans
Signal words: tomorrow, next…, soon, later

questions.q: Signal word for the simple past:
Which sentence is in the simple present?
Spot the error: 'If it will rain, we will cancel the trip.'
questions.explanation: In an 'if' clause use the simple present: 'If it rains …'.

questions.q: Choose the correct option: 'He usually ___ early, but yesterday he ___ late.'
Identify the error: 'The teacher teaches us yesterday.'

options: She does not goes to school.
She do not go to school.
She does not go to school.

questions.q: Choose: 'As soon as the bell ___, the students will leave.'
questions.explanation: Time clause takes the simple present: 'rings'.

questions.q: Rearrange: 'every / he / temple / the / visits / morning'
options: He visits the temple every morning.
He visit the temple every morning.
Every morning visits he the temple.
He the temple visits every morning.
questions.explanation: 'He visits the temple every morning.' is correct.

questions.q: Which option keeps the right sequence of tenses? 'He said that he ___ tired.'
questions.explanation: After a past reporting verb, the tense shifts back: 'was'.

outcomes: Form the simple present, past and future correctly
Add -s/-es to the verb for he/she/it in the present
Use the past form (V2) of regular and irregular verbs
Match each tense to its signal words

intro.en: Tense tells us the time of an action. The three simple tenses are the backbone of English: the simple present (she writes), the simple past (she wrote), and the simple future (she will write). Master these and most sentences fall into place.
intro.hi: काल (Tense) क्रिया का समय बताता है। तीन साधारण काल अंग्रेज़ी की रीढ़ हैं: simple present (she writes), simple past (she wrote), और simple future (she will write)। इन्हें समझ लें तो अधिकांश वाक्य सरल हो जाते हैं।

real_life.situation:
You introduce your daily life:

You: I study in Grade 6. Yesterday I visited my grandmother. Tomorrow I will join the cricket camp.
real_life.why: Three sentences, three times: a habit (present), a finished action (past), and a plan (future). Each verb form signals exactly when the action happens.

rule_box.html:
TenseFormExample
Simple PresentS + V1 (+s for he/she/it)She writes.
Simple PastS + V2She wrote.
Simple FutureS + will/shall + V1She will write.
rule_box.formula: Present: V1(+s) · Past: V2 · Future: will + V1
rule_box.example: Water boils at 100°C. We played yesterday. They will come soon.

quick_test.q: Which signal word goes with the simple past?
quick_test.explanation: 'yesterday' marks a finished action → simple past.

common_mistakes.note: Add -es for third-person singular in the present.
'next week' signals the future, not the past.

fill_l2.instructions: Use the correct tense (past or future) of the verb.

error_detection.sentence: She go to the market daily.
error_detection.correct: She goes to the market daily.

error_detection.sentence: The sun rose in the east every day.
error_detection.correct: The sun rises in the east every day.

sentence_correction.wrong: My father go to office by car.
sentence_correction.correct: My father goes to office by car.

sentence_correction.wrong: They will plays a match tomorrow.
sentence_correction.correct: They will play a match tomorrow.

sentence_correction.wrong: I eated my lunch at noon.
sentence_correction.correct: I ate my lunch at noon.

answers: She will write soon. → simple future

reading.passage: Every morning Neha waters the plants and feeds her dog. Yesterday she planted a new rose bush in the garden. "Tomorrow I will buy more seeds," she said. She believes that gardens make people happy, and she never forgets her morning routine.

questions.q: Find a simple present verb showing a habit.
questions.answer: waters (also 'feeds', 'never forgets') — daily routine, simple present.

questions.q: Which sentence is in the simple future?
questions.answer: "Tomorrow I will buy more seeds." — will + base verb.

speaking: I go to school every day.
The sun rises in the east.
We visited the museum last week.
He bought a new bicycle yesterday.

writing.prompt: Write five sentences about yesterday, today and tomorrow, using the simple past, present and future.
writing.example: I study daily. Yesterday I finished my project. Tomorrow I will start a new book.

micro_quiz.explanation: Universal truths use the simple present.

challenge.q: Identify the error: 'When I will reach home, I will call you.'
challenge.explanation: In a time clause with 'when', use the simple present: 'When I reach home …'.

challenge.q: Which sentence correctly uses the present for a timetable?
options: The train will leave at 6 a.m. daily.
The train leaves at 6 a.m. daily.
The train left at 6 a.m. daily.
challenge.explanation: Fixed timetables use the simple present: 'leaves'.
